# Skillbench 0.2.1

Skillbench 0.2.1 makes project inputs easier to understand and long-running CLI operations easier
to follow, while keeping explicit file and directory options available for automation.

## Changelog

### Clearer evaluations and CLI feedback

- `init` now creates a runnable release-checklist evaluation at
  `.skillbench/evals/development/default.yaml` and a richer multi-axis reference at
  `.skillbench/evals/examples/example.yaml`.
- The bundled qualitative assertions use the supported `llm-rubric.rubric` field and both starter
  YAML files are validated by the test suite.
- Interactive `eval`, `compare`, and `merge` commands list available evaluation files instead of
  asking for an opaque path. Explicit `--evals <file-or-directory>` inputs remain supported.
- Repetition prompts explain the speed, variance, and cost trade-off between 1, 2–3, and 10 runs.
- Evaluations, comparisons, qualitative judgments, merge planning, candidate tournaments, and
  holdout validation now show live progress for the active skill, case, and repetition.
- Empty path-like options are rejected, supplied text is trimmed, and invalid evaluations or report
  templates fail before later interactive questions are asked.

### Editable judging, reports, and merge output

- Qualitative judge behavior now lives in one richer `.skillbench/prompts/judge/SKILL.md`; the
  separate `judge-instruction.txt` file is no longer needed.
- Comparison reports are rendered from an editable `.skillbench/reports/comparison.md` template,
  selectable interactively or with `--report-template`. The selected template and its hash are
  included in result bundles.
- A skipped merge is displayed as a dedicated terminal callout with its reason and suggested next
  actions.
- The Web job form now targets the configured default evaluation file rather than the whole
  development directory.

### Distribution and releases

- Public npm tarballs no longer expose private `@skillbench/*` development workspace metadata.
- Tagged builds validate version-matched release notes before publication and create or update the
  GitHub Release from the same Markdown after both npm packages are published.

## Upgrade

### From 0.2.0 to 0.2.1

First update the package wherever it is installed, or use `npx @thisisjuke/skillbench@0.2.1` for
one-off commands. Existing `.skillbench` projects need a small layout migration. From the project
root, back up the current project files and run:

```sh
cp -a .skillbench .skillbench.backup-0.2.0
mkdir -p .skillbench/evals/examples .skillbench/prompts/judge .skillbench/reports
mv .skillbench/evals/development/example.yaml .skillbench/evals/development/default.yaml

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Thisisjuke/skills-benchmark/v0.2.1/packages/cli/defaults/project/evals/examples/example.yaml \
  -o .skillbench/evals/examples/example.yaml
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Thisisjuke/skills-benchmark/v0.2.1/packages/cli/defaults/project/skillbench/prompts/judge/SKILL.md \
  -o .skillbench/prompts/judge/SKILL.md
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Thisisjuke/skills-benchmark/v0.2.1/packages/cli/defaults/project/skillbench/reports/comparison.md \
  -o .skillbench/reports/comparison.md
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Thisisjuke/skills-benchmark/v0.2.1/packages/cli/defaults/project/skillbench/assets.yaml \
  -o .skillbench/assets.yaml

rm -f .skillbench/judge/SKILL.md .skillbench/prompts/judge-instruction.txt
rmdir .skillbench/judge 2>/dev/null || true
```

The 0.2.1 configuration schema supplies the new evaluation and report-template paths when they are
absent, so existing runner and output settings remain valid. To make those defaults explicit, add
the following keys while preserving the rest of `.skillbench/config.yaml`:

```yaml
eval:
  path: .skillbench/evals/development/default.yaml
  repeat: 1
  timeoutMs: 180000

reports:
  markdown: true
  template: .skillbench/reports/comparison.md
```

Finish by validating the migrated project:

```sh
npx @thisisjuke/skillbench@0.2.1 doctor
```

If you had customized the former eval or judge files, compare them with
`.skillbench.backup-0.2.0` and reapply those changes to the new locations.
